records.title: Drift Protocol loses about $285 million in privileged-access exploit
records.summary: Drift Protocol was drained of about $285 million after attackers obtained privileged control and used a worthless artificially priced token as collateral to withdraw real assets. Drift's own recovery update confirms the April 1 incident and a subsequent user-recovery program.
records.significance: The exploit became one of 2026's largest DeFi losses and a major example of operational-security and privileged-access risk rather than a simple smart-contract coding bug.
records.notes: Chainalysis says preliminary indicators are consistent with DPRK operations, but formal attribution was still pending in its report; do not present DPRK attribution as settled fact.

records.title: Liquid Network exploit creates about 4,000 unbacked LBTC and drains roughly 4,000 BTC
records.summary: A vulnerability in Elements' rangeproof verification cache allowed an attacker to create approximately 4,000 unbacked LBTC on Liquid and use the normal peg-out process to withdraw about 4,000 real BTC. The attacker later returned 3,400 BTC, while Blockstream patched the vulnerability and reorganized the invalid chain history.
records.significance: The incident was an extraordinary Bitcoin-sidechain failure: a consensus-validation cache bug enabled unbacked sidechain assets to be converted into real Bitcoin reserves, forcing a coordinated network halt and recovery.

sources.title: Blockstream — Liquid Network Security Incident Assessment

records.title: Physical wrench attacks against crypto holders reach record pace
records.summary: Chainalysis documented 46 violent crypto-related incidents globally through late June 2026, with more than $30 million successfully stolen. France recorded a particularly sharp increase in reported attacks.
records.significance: The trend marks a shift from purely digital key theft toward physical coercion becoming a material personal-security risk for visible crypto holders.

sources.title: Chainalysis — Violent Wrench Attacks Targeting Crypto Holders

records.notes: Trend/context record, not a single incident. Likely book/archive material rather than an automatic physical card.
